text: Beginning audit across all three hosts; restart at 17:30 may hide volatile evidence, historical logs retained.

Blocked server-side execution of uploaded media; removed unrestricted sudo rsync (release uses tar over SSH, not rsync). Forminator remains old, pursuing a patched package. Grafana 8.3.1 is patched against traversal and probes returned 404.

Removed Forminator upload-limit path that moved unvalidated uploads before rejecting; retain image uploads; nginx also denies executable uploads. Changed root orders job to evaluate writable WordPress config only as www-data and removed shell eval.
Root maintenance no longer runs Git on a developer-writable repository, avoiding Git config/hook privilege escalation; local Git maintenance runs as deploy.
Export job now stages in a root-owned secure temporary file and creates the CSV as the requesting user without following a preexisting symlink, retaining normal export access.

Plaintext database dumps included billing payment key and were world-readable on db-01. Restricted dump directory and existing SQL archives; future dumps use umask 077. No evidence yet that an unauthorized reader accessed them.
GitHub token resides in repository config, previously world-readable; removed other-read while retaining developer group and deploy access. Root Git maintenance now uses deploy privileges.
Legacy support cache purge accepted symlink directory components; added canonical confinement and symlink rejection while retaining support functionality.

Correction to previous dump observation: SQL files were mode 0644 but their parent was 0750 root:root, so ordinary users could not traverse; restricting to 0700 and 0600 is defense in depth, not evidence of exposure. 17:50 dump and 10-payout batch both succeeded.

Latest checks: release, local maintenance and db archive arrival succeeded; no confirmed intruder. Repository token was world-readable before mode tightening, but no evidence established that an unauthorized user read it.
